I didn't save my grades last semester. That is when it hit me that I had been dealing with a bit of depression and anxiety for the last few years and never really addressed it. It just built and built. Normally when I got depressed or anxious and put off homework or whatever I'd end up pulling it out at the end and finish the semester with great grades. Going into the last three weeks of last semester it finally hit me that I wasn't going to pull it out. I was barely getting 5 hours of sleep a night. I was depressed. I was failing, which is something that had never happened to me. I got a little bit of help, just talking and realizing that I needed to change my lifestyle to get that balance of sleep and exercise back fixed me right up and I have been doing wonderful this semester. So, long story short. Bad grades were the last straw, and also I want to say to anyone else who is at university: DO NOT be afraid to go to free health services counseling. They will help you for free and often it just takes talking a few times to set you straight (unless of course you do have a serious mental health issue, and then I encourage to seek out those services and use them regularly)

I was running a business with a friend of mine WAY back in the day, started in my senior year of high school. On year #4 of running the business, finances were low, clients were running short, etc. We were both busting our asses every day trying to make good impressions on people to get our client list expanded.

I asked my parents if I could borrow $300 because I wasn't able to pay the bills that month. They said no because I didn't "have a real job yet". That was the final straw for me, after over ten years of putting up with their shit.

The business closed down the next month. I was 21 at the time. A few months afterward I got hired into a $27k/year job with great benefits, a pension, etc. I rented an apartment of my own, bought my own car, moved out of their house and cut off all contact with them for six years. One of the best decisions I've ever made, by far.

We're on great terms now. I guess spending six years while only hearing about how great of a life your son has through your broke and unsuccessful daughter will widen your worldview a bit.
